checked_sources: Polich 2007 (Europe PMC record and abstract; full text could not be opened: Europe PMC fullTextXML returned HTTP 500, PMC/PMC-PDF/europepmc.org/ScienceDirect blocked by CAPTCHA, Cloudflare or client error; instead the Europe PMC full-text index was probed with exact-phrase BODY: queries restricted to PMCID:PMC2715154, which reports 1 hit when a phrase occurs in the body and 0 otherwise)
Farwell & Donchin 1988 (Europe PMC record and abstract)
Vialatte et al. 2010 (Europe PMC record and abstract only; closed access, no repository copy per OpenAlex, ScienceDirect and CORE blocked)
Chavarriaga, Sobolewski & Millán 2014 (full text, Europe PMC fullTextXML of PMC4106211)
evidence_location: P300 part, Polich 2007: abstract ('P3b originates from temporal-parietal activity associated with attention'); body phrases confirmed present by the Europe PMC full-text index: 'P3b has a parietal maximum', 'positive-going waveform', 'midline electrodes', 'Fz, Cz, Pz', 'increases in magnitude from the frontal to parietal', 'two-stimulus oddball', 'infrequent target', 'frequent standard', 'P300 peak latency', 'of 250-500 ms'; absent: '300 ms', 'about 300', 'approximately 300', 'around 300', 'attended'. Speller part, Farwell & Donchin 1988: abstract ('This detection is achieved by repeatedly flashing rows and columns of the matrix. When the elements containing the chosen character are flashed, a P300 is elicited'). SSVEP part, Vialatte et al. 2010: abstract only, which says SSVEPs are studied with scalp EEG, are 'steady-state evoked activity' of the visual pathway and drive 'SSVEP-driven brain-computer interface (BCI) systems'; it does not mention the occipital cortex, the stimulation frequency, harmonics, or selecting one of several flickering targets by looking at it. ErrP part, Chavarriaga et al. 2014: section 2 'Error-related brain activity' (ERN 'over fronto-central scalp areas at about 50-100 ms after a subject's erroneous response', followed by 'a centro-parietal positive deflection (Pe)'; FRN 'between 200 and 300 ms after feedback onset'; in BMI feedback an initial positive peak at about 200 ms, a larger negativity at about 250 ms, a positivity at about 320 ms); section 1 'Introduction' (ErrPs 'can be reliably decoded on a single-trial basis'; decoding lets 'the system take corrective actions, e.g., by preventing the erroneous command from being fully executed or reverting its outcome'); section 4 'Error-related potentials as a corrective signal'.
quote: appearing over fronto-central scalp areas at about 50–100 ms after a subject's erroneous response
discrepancy: (1) Latency: Polich 2007 gives the P300 peak latency as a range, 250-500 ms (phrase 'of 250-500 ms' present, no '300 ms', 'about 300' or similar anywhere in the body), so 'about 300 ms' is a nominal value not stated by the source. (2) The parietal maximum, the midline gradient (amplitude increasing from frontal to parietal over Fz, Cz, Pz) and the oddball 'infrequent target' are supported by phrase hits, but I could not read the full sentences; 'attended' does not occur (the paper uses 'attention'). (3) SSVEP: none of the specific statements (occipital cortex; periodic at the flicker frequency and its harmonics; looking at one of several flickering targets selects it) could be checked: only Vialatte's abstract was accessible and it contains none of them; it supports only that SSVEPs drive BCI systems. (4) ErrP: fully supported; one dropped nuance: the positivity that follows the ERN is centro-parietal (Pe), and in BMI feedback the error-minus-correct waveform starts with a positive peak at about 200 ms before the negativity at about 250 ms. (5) Speller: supported by the Farwell & Donchin abstract (rows and columns of a character matrix flashed; a P300 when the row or column containing the chosen character flashes).
suggested_fix: P300 (P3b): 'a positive wave largest over the parietal midline, peaking roughly 250 to 500 ms (nominally about 300 ms) after an infrequent target stimulus in an oddball task'. If the figure must say 'about 300 ms', add a source that states it (Polich 2007 gives 250-500 ms). SSVEP: keep the wording but either cite a source whose text states the occipital origin, the response at the stimulation frequency and its harmonics, and target selection by gaze (an open review would let it be verified), or mark this part partially verified pending access to Vialatte's full text. ErrP: optionally 'followed by a centro-parietal positivity (Pe)'.
bibliographic_issues: None found. All four DOIs resolve (three to linkinghub.elsevier.com, the Frontiers one to the article page). Europe PMC confirms: Polich J, Clin Neurophysiol 118(10):2128-2148, 2007, PMID 17573239, PMCID PMC2715154; Farwell LA, Donchin E, Electroencephalogr Clin Neurophysiol 70(6):510-523, 1988, PMID 2461285 (the DOI search returned nothing but the title search returned the record carrying that DOI); Vialatte FB, Maurice M, Dauwels J, Cichocki A, Prog Neurobiol 90(4):418-438, 2010, PMID 19963032 (OpenAlex lists the online year 2009; the issue is 2010); Chavarriaga R, Sobolewski A, Millán JdR, Front Neurosci 8:208, 2014, PMID 25100937, PMCID PMC4106211 (the PMC record also carries page numbers 480-488, but the article number 208 is the standard citation).
